name: Axiom Systems Cerberus Intrusion Deck
description: A compact cyberdeck designed for offensive network intrusion, containing three independent processing cores that can simultaneously attack different security layers of a target system. The Cerberus runs Axiom's proprietary penetration suite — a library of exploit packages, cryptographic attack tools, and social engineering AI modules that adapt to target defenses in real-time. The deck interfaces directly with the operator's neural implant for speed-of-thought interaction and includes a hardware firewall that isolates the operator's neural interface from counterattack. Its triple-core architecture allows parallel attacks that overwhelm security systems designed to handle single-vector intrusions.
story_hooks: A Cerberus deck has been recovered with its attack logs intact, revealing that the operator penetrated a system they should not have been able to crack — the logs show a fourth attack vector that the hardware should not support.
Axiom's Penetration Suite has been updated with a backdoor that reports all successful intrusions back to Axiom — operators using the deck are unknowingly sharing their targets with its manufacturer.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular cyberdeck with a tri-partitioned design reflecting its triple-core architecture. The main body tapers from a wider processing hub to narrower interface nodes. Aggressive, purposeful industrial aesthetic with exposed heat dissipation vanes. Asymmetrical—suggests active, directed energy outward.
physical_description.weight_description: 400g—substantial but wearable. Requires carrying strap or secure mounting point to prevent cable stress on neural jack.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum chassis with reinforced graphene composite internal structure. Thermal pyrite matrix for heat dissipation.
physical_description.finish: Brushed satin black with mirror-polished accent bevels. Three vertical cooling vanes show anodized copper heat-sink channels beneath semi-transparent protective resin.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte charcoal black. Accents: copper heat-dissipation traces, electric cyan status indicators, white operational text. Subtle iridescent oil-slick shimmer on cooling vanes under extreme lighting.
physical_description.interface_elements: Dual 1.2-inch OLED side-screens (attack status for each of 2 visible cores), recessed membrane keypad (7×4, unlabeled—muscle-memory operation), neural jack (proprietary Axiom MicroSync, exposed and hardened), three micro-USB diagnostic ports (color-coded: red/blue/gold for each processing core), haptic feedback pad running the device's left edge
distinctive_features: Three distinct processing bumps along the spine—visible core separation internally through smoked transparent sections
Pulsing neural interface jack with soft blue status ring (idle/active/locked states)
Copper heat-pipe geometry etched into casing—functional and aesthetic
Small spinning heatsink fan vent (rarely visible, indicates sustained attack mode)
Faint 3-matrix grid pattern laser-etched across surface—security code that shifts under certain wavelengths
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: AXIOM SYSTEMS logo (stylized Cerberus silhouette—three-headed dog) stamped in white on top-right corner. Serial number holographically embedded (shifts between visible and hidden). Regulatory stamps for GLMZ neural hardware compliance (small Φ symbol indicating Tier 3+ pricing tier).
physical_description.condition_typical: In active use: cooling vanes glow faintly warm to touch, status indicators cycle rapid cyan pulses, minor scuff marks from quick-deploy operations, possibly mounted to reinforced wrist rig with shock-absorbing gel pads and Faraday shielding wrap.
